# Method for Purifying Acrylic Acid Derivatives

## Field and Objective of the Invention

The present invention aims to provide a method for efficiently purifying an acrylic acid derivative represented by Formula (I) by effectively removing an alcohol, represented by Formula (II), from a composition that contains both substances. The removal of residual alcohol from such compositions has long posed a challenge in achieving high-purity acrylic acid derivatives, and the present invention addresses this need through a novel and effective purification approach.

## Compounds Involved

The acrylic acid derivative to be purified is represented by Formula (I), in which the substituents R¹ and R² may each independently be an alkyl group, a fluoroalkyl group, an optionally substituted aryl group, a halogen atom, or a hydrogen atom. This flexibility in the definition of R¹ and R² allows the method to be applied to a broad range of acrylic acid derivatives.

The alcohol to be eliminated is represented by Formula (II), namely R⁴—OH, wherein R⁴ denotes a C₁₋₆ alkyl group. Such alcohols are commonly present as impurities in compositions containing acrylic acid derivatives, and their effective removal is essential for obtaining a purified product.

## Purification Method

The purification method comprises a step, referred to as Step A, in which Composition A—containing both the acrylic acid derivative (I) and the alcohol (II)—is brought into contact with an acid anhydride. Through this contact, the alcohol (II) is converted into a corresponding ester compound by reaction with the acid anhydride.

## Basis for Efficient Separation

The ester compound generated in Step A has a boiling point higher than that of the acrylic acid derivative (I). This difference in boiling points enables the acrylic acid derivative to be readily separated from the ester compound, for example by distillation. As a result, the alcohol, which would otherwise be difficult to remove directly, is effectively eliminated in the form of a higher-boiling ester, thereby allowing the acrylic acid derivative (I) to be purified efficiently and with high purity.

# Method for Purifying Acrylic Acid Derivatives by Removal of Alcohol Contaminants

## Background of the Invention

Acrylic acid derivatives are valuable industrial compounds widely employed in the manufacture of polymers, adhesives, coatings, and a broad range of specialty chemicals. However, the practical utility of these derivatives depends heavily on their purity. During synthesis, storage, or handling, acrylic acid derivatives frequently become contaminated with residual alcohols. These alcohol impurities can adversely affect subsequent reactions, degrade product quality, and interfere with polymerization and other downstream processes.

A persistent challenge in the field has been the difficulty of separating alcohol contaminants from acrylic acid derivatives. In many cases, the boiling points of the alcohol impurities are close to those of the target compounds, rendering conventional separation techniques—such as simple distillation—inefficient, energy-intensive, or incapable of achieving the desired level of purity. There remains, therefore, a need for a reliable and efficient method of removing alcohol contaminants from acrylic acid derivative compositions.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses this challenge by providing an effective method for purifying acrylic acid derivatives through the selective removal of alcohol contaminants. According to the invention, a composition containing the acrylic acid derivative together with one or more alcohol impurities is brought into contact with an acid anhydride. The acid anhydride reacts preferentially with the alcohol, converting it into a corresponding ester compound.

The ester compound thus formed possesses a substantially higher boiling point than the original alcohol. This significant difference in boiling point between the newly generated ester and the target acrylic acid derivative permits the two to be readily separated by conventional means, such as distillation. As a result, the alcohol contaminant is effectively removed from the composition, and the desired acrylic acid derivative can be recovered in high purity.

## Advantages of the Invention

By transforming a difficult-to-separate alcohol impurity into a higher-boiling ester, the invention converts a challenging separation problem into a straightforward one. This approach offers several benefits:

- **Improved separation efficiency**, since the boiling point gap between the target derivative and the converted impurity is widened.
- **Enhanced product purity**, as alcohol contaminants that would otherwise remain in the product are effectively eliminated.
- **Practical applicability**, because the method relies on readily available acid anhydrides and standard separation equipment.

In this way, the invention provides an efficient, reliable, and practical means of purifying acrylic acid derivatives, thereby overcoming the limitations of conventional purification techniques.

# The Power of a Formula

**The** concept of a formula sits at the heart of nearly every scientific and mathematical discipline. Whether we are calculating the area of a circle, predicting the motion of planets, or balancing a chemical equation, a formula provides us with a reliable, repeatable path from a known set of inputs to a meaningful result.

**This** reliability is precisely what makes formulas so valuable. Instead of solving the same problem from scratch every single time, we can encode the underlying relationship into a compact expression and apply it universally. A formula transforms a complex idea into a simple, actionable tool that anyone can use, provided they understand its variables and limitations.

## Why Formulas Matter

**The** beauty of a well-constructed formula lies in its efficiency. Consider Einstein's famous equation, E = mc². In just a few symbols, it captures a profound truth about the relationship between energy and mass—one that reshaped our understanding of the physical universe. **This** kind of elegant compression is what scientists and mathematicians strive to achieve.

Formulas also serve as a shared language. **The** notation may look intimidating at first, but once learned, it allows people across countries and cultures to communicate precise ideas without ambiguity.

## A Tool for Everyday Life

**This** usefulness extends far beyond the laboratory. From calculating interest on a loan to converting temperatures, formulas quietly power the decisions we make every day. **The** next time you use one, take a moment to appreciate the centuries of human ingenuity distilled into that single, powerful expression.

# Patent Application Draft Sections

## Problem to be Solved by the Invention

Acrylic acid derivatives, particularly acrylic acid esters (such as alkyl acrylates and alkyl methacrylates), are typically produced through esterification reactions between acrylic acid or methacrylic acid and a corresponding alcohol. In such production processes, the alcohol reactant is often used in excess to drive the esterification reaction toward completion and to improve the conversion rate of the acid component.

As a consequence of this manufacturing approach, the resulting acrylic acid derivative product frequently contains a certain amount of residual, unreacted alcohol. Even when conventional purification techniques such as distillation are employed, it is difficult to completely remove this residual alcohol. This difficulty is particularly pronounced when the boiling point of the residual alcohol is close to that of the target acrylic acid derivative, or when the alcohol and the acrylic acid derivative form an azeotrope, rendering separation by distillation impractical or economically unfeasible.

The presence of residual alcohol in the purified product poses several problems. The residual alcohol can act as an impurity that degrades product quality and reduces purity below specifications required for high-performance applications. Furthermore, in downstream applications such as polymerization, the residual alcohol may participate in undesirable side reactions, interfere with the polymerization process, act as a chain transfer agent that adversely affects molecular weight control, or otherwise compromise the properties of the resulting polymer.

Accordingly, there has been a need for a method that can effectively and efficiently reduce the residual alcohol content in acrylic acid derivatives, particularly a method capable of removing residual alcohol that is difficult to separate by conventional distillation.

## Solution to Problem

The present inventors have conducted extensive studies to solve the above-described problems and have found that residual alcohol contained in an acrylic acid derivative can be effectively removed by adding an acid anhydride to the composition containing the acrylic acid derivative and the residual alcohol. The acid anhydride selectively reacts with the residual alcohol to convert the alcohol into a corresponding ester and a corresponding carboxylic acid, thereby consuming the free alcohol. The resulting reaction products differ in physical properties (such as boiling point) from the target acrylic acid derivative and can therefore be readily separated, or alternatively remain as innocuous components that do not adversely affect the intended use of the product.

The present invention has been completed based on these findings, and includes the following embodiments:

**[1]** A method for purifying an acrylic acid derivative, comprising a step of adding an acid anhydride to a composition containing an acrylic acid derivative and a residual alcohol, and reacting the acid anhydride with the residual alcohol to reduce the content of the residual alcohol in the composition.

**[2]** The purification method according to [1], wherein the acrylic acid derivative is an ester of acrylic acid or methacrylic acid.

**[3]** The purification method according to [1] or [2], wherein the residual alcohol is an alcohol used as a raw material in the production of the acrylic acid derivative.

**[4]** The purification method according to any one of [1] to [3], wherein the acid anhydride is a carboxylic acid anhydride, preferably acetic anhydride.

**[5]** The purification method according to any one of [1] to [4], wherein the acid anhydride is added in an amount equal to or in excess of the stoichiometric amount relative to the residual alcohol.

**[6]** The purification method according to any one of [1] to [5], further comprising, after the reacting step, a step of removing at least one of the reaction product and the unreacted acid anhydride from the composition, for example by distillation.

According to the present invention, residual alcohol that is difficult to remove by conventional means such as distillation—including alcohol having a boiling point close to that of the acrylic acid derivative or forming an azeotrope therewith—can be efficiently reduced or removed. As a result, a high-purity acrylic acid derivative can be obtained, and problems attributable to residual alcohol in downstream applications such as polymerization can be suppressed.

---

*Note: The bracketed embodiment numbering and specific examples (e.g., acetic anhydride) are provided as drafting placeholders and should be reviewed and tailored to align with the actual claims, working examples, and technical scope of your specific invention.*

# Patent Summary

## Method for Separating a C1-6 Alcohol from a Composition Comprising an Acrylic Acid Derivative

### Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a process for the efficient separation and recovery of a C₁₋₆ alcohol from a composition containing an acrylic acid derivative of Formula (I). More particularly, the invention concerns converting the low-boiling alcohol into a higher-boiling ester to facilitate its separation from the acrylic acid derivative by conventional distillation or phase-separation techniques.

### Background

In many industrial processes involving acrylic acid derivatives—such as (meth)acrylate polymerization, transesterification, and hydrolysis reactions—residual C₁₋₆ alcohols (e.g., methanol, ethanol, propanol, butanol, or their isomers) remain present in the product stream. Because certain of these alcohols form azeotropes with reaction components or exhibit boiling points close to those of other constituents, their direct removal by simple distillation is inefficient, energy-intensive, and may promote unwanted polymerization of the acrylic species.

### Summary of the Invention

The invention provides a method comprising the following principal steps:

**1. Providing a Composition**
A composition is provided comprising:
- an acrylic acid derivative of Formula (I); and
- a C₁₋₆ alcohol to be separated.

**Formula (I):**

$$CH_2=C(R_1)-C(=O)-X-R_2$$

wherein:
- **R₁** is hydrogen or a C₁₋₄ alkyl group (e.g., methyl for methacrylic derivatives);
- **X** is oxygen (–O–) or an amino linkage (–NR₃–);
- **R₂** is hydrogen, a C₁₋₆ alkyl, an aryl, or a substituted derivative thereof.

**2. Esterification (Boiling-Point Elevation) Step**
The C₁₋₆ alcohol is selectively reacted with an **esterifying agent** having a boiling point and reactivity chosen such that the resulting ester possesses a boiling point substantially higher than that of the free alcohol. Suitable esterifying agents include:
- higher carboxylic acids (e.g., C₈₋₁₈ fatty acids);
- carboxylic acid anhydrides;
- acyl halides.

The esterification converts the volatile alcohol (R–OH) into a higher-boiling ester (R–O–C(=O)–R'), thereby increasing the boiling-point differential between the alcohol-derived species and the acrylic acid derivative of Formula (I).

**3. Separation Step**
The higher-boiling ester is separated from the acrylic acid derivative by:
- fractional distillation, wherein the acrylic acid derivative and/or lighter components are removed overhead while the higher-boiling ester is retained in the bottoms (or vice versa, depending on the relative volatilities); or
- liquid–liquid phase separation, where applicable.

**4. Optional Recovery Step**
The higher-boiling ester may optionally be **hydrolyzed or transesterified** to regenerate and recover the original C₁₋₆ alcohol and the esterifying agent for recycle.

### Advantages

- **Improved separation efficiency:** Converting a low-boiling alcohol into a higher-boiling ester enlarges the boiling-point differential, avoiding azeotrope formation and enabling clean separation.
- **Reduced energy consumption:** Distillation is achieved under milder conditions with fewer theoretical stages.
- **Preservation of the acrylic species:** Milder processing conditions minimize thermally induced or radical polymerization of the acrylic acid derivative of Formula (I), optionally in the presence of a polymerization inhibitor (e.g., hydroquinone, MEHQ, or phenothiazine).
- **Alcohol recovery:** The alcohol can be regenerated and recycled, improving overall process economy.

### Representative Embodiment

In one embodiment, a stream comprising methyl methacrylate (Formula (I), R₁ = CH₃, X = O, R₂ = CH₃) and residual methanol is treated with lauric acid under acid catalysis to convert the methanol into methyl laurate (b.p. ~ 262 °C). The high-boiling methyl laurate is readily separated from the methyl methacrylate by distillation, and subsequent hydrolysis regenerates methanol for reuse.

---

*This summary is intended for illustrative drafting purposes and should be reviewed and adapted by a qualified patent professional prior to filing.*

# Purification of Acrylic Acid Esters via Acid Anhydride Treatment

## Technical Problem

Acrylic acid esters (I) are typically produced through **esterification reactions** between (meth)acrylic acid and a corresponding alcohol. A persistent challenge in this manufacturing process is that the crude product contains **residual free alcohol (II)** as a contaminant.

This residual alcohol is problematic because:

- It is often difficult to remove by **distillation alone**, particularly when the alcohol and the target ester have **similar boiling points** or form **azeotropes**
- The presence of free hydroxyl groups can cause **stability, quality, and reactivity issues** in downstream applications (e.g., coatings, adhesives, polymerization processes)
- Conventional purification may require harsh conditions that risk **unwanted polymerization** of the acrylate double bond

## Inventive Method

The invention solves this problem by **chemically converting** the contaminating alcohol rather than attempting physical separation of the alcohol itself.

**The method involves:**

1. Adding an **acid anhydride** to the crude ester mixture containing the alcohol impurity (II)
2. The acid anhydride reacts selectively with the free alcohol's **hydroxyl group** to form an ester and a carboxylic acid byproduct
3. The alcohol is thereby transformed into a **higher-boiling ester derivative** and a **carboxylic acid**, both of which can now be **readily separated by distillation** from the target product (I)

This approach effectively removes the alcohol impurity by increasing the boiling-point difference between contaminants and the desired product, allowing clean isolation of the purified acrylic acid ester (I).

## Substituent Definitions for Formula (I)

| Substituent | Definition |
|-------------|------------|
| **R¹** | Hydrogen atom or a methyl group (i.e., distinguishing **acrylate** from **methacrylate**) |
| **R²** | Hydrogen atom or a methyl group |
| **R³** | An organic residue, typically a **substituted or unsubstituted alkyl, cycloalkyl, aryl, or aralkyl group** (the ester alcohol-derived moiety) |
| **X** | A **divalent linking group**, such as an alkylene chain, oxygen-containing (e.g., polyether/oxyalkylene), or other spacer connecting the ester functionality to R³ |

---

**Note:** Since these definitions and the exact scope of the claims are specific to your particular invention, I'd recommend confirming that the substituent ranges (especially for **R³** and **X**) match your actual worked examples and the intended breadth of your claims. Would you like help drafting the formal claim language or the detailed example section?

# Summary of the Invention

The present invention relates to a process for purifying an acrylic acid derivative composition containing alcohol impurities. More particularly, the invention provides a method by which alcohol impurities present in an acrylic acid derivative composition are converted into higher-boiling esters through reaction with an acid anhydride, thereby facilitating their subsequent separation and removal by distillation.

Acrylic acid derivatives, including acrylic acid, methacrylic acid, and their corresponding esters, are valuable industrial intermediates used in the production of polymers, coatings, adhesives, and superabsorbent materials. In many commercial preparations, these compositions contain residual alcohol impurities that are difficult to remove by conventional distillation. This difficulty arises because certain alcohol impurities exhibit boiling points that are close to, or form azeotropes with, the desired acrylic acid derivative product, resulting in incomplete separation and reduced product purity.

It has now been found that such alcohol impurities can be effectively removed by treating the acrylic acid derivative composition with an acid anhydride under conditions sufficient to esterify the alcohol. In accordance with the invention, the acid anhydride reacts selectively with the hydroxyl-bearing alcohol impurities to form the corresponding ester and carboxylic acid byproduct. The ester so formed possesses a boiling point that differs substantially from that of the acrylic acid derivative, thereby enabling the ester to be readily separated from the desired product by distillation.

In one aspect, the invention provides a purification process comprising: (a) providing an acrylic acid derivative composition containing one or more alcohol impurities; (b) contacting the composition with an acid anhydride under conditions effective to esterify at least a portion of the alcohol impurities and produce a corresponding ester; and (c) distilling the resulting mixture to separate the purified acrylic acid derivative from the ester and any remaining reaction byproducts.

The process of the present invention offers several advantages over conventional purification techniques. By chemically converting the troublesome alcohol impurities into esters having distinctly different volatility characteristics, the invention overcomes the limitations associated with close-boiling components and azeotrope formation. As a result, the process affords an acrylic acid derivative product of high purity in an efficient and economical manner, while employing readily available reagents and standard distillation equipment.

These and other features and advantages of the invention will become more fully apparent from the following detailed description.

# Method for Facilitating Separation of an Alcohol Component

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a method for separating an alcohol component from a composition, and more particularly to a method wherein an alcohol is chemically transformed to raise its boiling point to facilitate separation.

## SUMMARY OF THE METHOD

A method for treating a composition, said method comprising:

**Step A** of contacting a composition comprising an acrylic acid derivative represented by formula (I) and an alcohol represented by formula R⁴-OH (II) with an acid anhydride,

wherein said contacting effects esterification of at least a portion of said alcohol (II) with said acid anhydride to form an ester of said alcohol,

whereby a boiling point of said alcohol component is raised relative to a boiling point of said alcohol (II) prior to said esterification, thereby facilitating separation of said alcohol component from said acrylic acid derivative (I).

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

In one embodiment, the acrylic acid derivative (I) may comprise a compound bearing an acryloyl or methacryloyl moiety, optionally substituted, and the alcohol (II) comprises a compound of formula R⁴-OH, wherein R⁴ represents a substituted or unsubstituted hydrocarbyl group.

In a preferred embodiment, said acid anhydride is selected from the group consisting of aliphatic acid anhydrides, aromatic acid anhydrides, and combinations thereof, non-limiting examples including acetic anhydride, propionic anhydride, and phthalic anhydride.

In Step A, the acid anhydride is provided in an amount sufficient to convert at least a portion, and preferably substantially all, of the alcohol (II) present in said composition to the corresponding ester derivative, said ester derivative having a boiling point higher than that of the unreacted alcohol (II).

In a further embodiment, the method further comprises:

**Step B** of separating the higher-boiling ester derivative formed in Step A from the acrylic acid derivative (I), for example by distillation, fractional distillation, evaporation, or an equivalent separation operation.

Without wishing to be bound by theory, it is believed that the conversion of the relatively low-boiling alcohol (II) to a corresponding higher-boiling ester enlarges the difference in boiling points between the alcohol-derived component and the acrylic acid derivative (I), thereby permitting more efficient and/or more complete separation than would be achievable in the presence of the free alcohol (II).

In certain embodiments, Step A is conducted at a temperature and for a period sufficient to substantially complete the esterification, optionally in the presence of a catalyst and/or a polymerization inhibitor to suppress undesired polymerization of the acrylic acid derivative (I).

---
